doc: Robot body profiles (docs/design/TIER1_EMBODIMENT.md section 3.1 with the TIER1_INTEGRATION 1.2 changes). A robot selects one with robot.body_profile; 'inherits' deep-merges a parent profile and robot.profile_overrides deep-merges over the result for one episode. humanoid_v1 reproduces every robot number the simulator used before the body model. 'sources' says where each number comes from; the fidelity is P-approx.

humanoid_v1.doc: 60 kg, 1.6 m general-purpose humanoid (Optimus / Figure / Apollo class)

humanoid_compact.doc: 35 kg, 1.3 m compact humanoid (Unitree G1 / Booster T1 class)

mobile_manipulator.doc: wheeled base with a torso and two arms (TIAGo++ / Stretch-like class); no stairs

sources.mass_kg, height_m: humanoid_v1 keeps the 60 kg and 1.6 m the simulator already used (navigation_robot ROBOT_MASS_KG, schema height_m); current general-purpose humanoids are 57-73 kg and 1.6-1.75 m (Optimus Gen 2 about 57 kg, Figure 02 70 kg, Apollo 73 kg, Digit 65 kg). Compact: Unitree G1 35 kg, 1.32 m. Mobile manipulator: TIAGo++ about 70 kg, 1.1-1.45 m.
sources.width_m, sideways_width_m: Shoulder breadth 0.5 m (schema default), 0.36 m turned sideways (torso depth plus arm clearance); the wheeled base is round, so both are its 0.55 m diameter.
sources.support_half_m: Static support half-length for body.stability_margin: half a humanoid foot (0.24 m long; 0.20 m for the compact one), the base radius less its bumper for the wheeled robot (0.25 m).
sources.reach_m: Standing overhead reach 1.85 m (geometry.DEFAULT_REACH_M); about 1.16 x height, as for adults.
sources.eye_height_m: Head camera at 94 % of a 1.6 m robot's height (1.50 m standing), TIER1_INTEGRATION 1.2. Crouching and sitting about 0.95 m; the kernel's kneel is the low look-under posture with the torso pitched down (0.60 m); lying 0.30 m. The wheeled base cannot crouch or kneel: those postures only tilt its torso (0.90 m).
sources.carry: One-hand loads ride at elbow height with the forearm level (1.0 m for 1.6 m tall), two-hand bulky loads at the hip (0.85 m), their near face 0.35 m in front of the body axis (TIER1_INTEGRATION 1.2).
sources.max_hand_kg, max_mass_kg: 8 kg per hand and 20 kg with both hands near the body are the simulator's existing payload rule (core pick_up); Digit is rated 16 kg, Figure 02 20 kg, Apollo 25 kg. Compact: Unitree G1 arms carry about 2-3 kg each, so 4 / 10 kg is the optimistic end.
sources.push_n: 220 N sustained horizontal push (manipulation ROBOT_PUSH_N): friction-limited by the feet, 0.37 x 60 kg x 9.81 m/s2 on a hard floor. Compact scaled by mass (120 N).
sources.pull_n: 180 N: pulling leans the body back over the heels, so it is limited about 20 % below the push (TIER1_PHYSICS). Compact scaled by the same ratio (100 N).
sources.wrist_nm: 6 N m twisting torque (manipulation ROBOT_WRIST_TORQUE_NM): enough for jar lids (2-5 N m) and stuck caps; an adult manages 10-15 N m.
sources.grippers.hand: Humanoid hand: 150 N power grip and 30 N fingertip pinch (an adult's power grip is 300-500 N, tip pinch 50-70 N); a power grasp needs an item of at least 15 mm to wrap, fingertip pads cannot oppose below 2 mm; positioning to 2 mm is typical of visual servoing with humanoid hands; rubber fingertip pads give mu 0.8 on dry objects.
sources.grippers.parallel: Parallel-jaw gripper: 140 N peak (Franka Hand 70 N continuous, 140 N peak; Robotiq 2F-85 20-235 N), the same force in a pinch, closes on items of 1 mm, positions to 1 mm, hard pads mu 0.6, and cannot lift paper-thin flat items off a surface except by their edges or by scooping.
sources.battery_wh: 2.4 kWh: Optimus Gen 2 2.3 kWh, Figure 02 2.25 kWh; a swappable pack of this size weighs about 14 kg (TIER1_DECISIONS). The compact humanoid carries a pack in proportion to its mass (1 kWh, about 6 kg).
sources.thresholds_pct: Low 20 % and reserve 15 % are the usual return-to-dock levels of consumer robots and navigation_robot's BATTERY_RESERVE_PCT; critical 5 % starts the firmware's limp mode; cutoff 0 % on the gauge (the BMS keeps a hidden buffer below it, energy_buffer_pct); the robot powers back on at 3 % so it cannot die again at once.
sources.power_w: Awake idle 115 W standing = 70 W compute and sensors (Jetson AGX Orin class 15-60 W plus cameras, lidar, network and BMS) + 45 W to hold balance; Tesla reported about 100 W for Optimus at rest. Crouching costs more (bent knees carry higher joint torques), kneeling and sitting less, lying needs only brakes, standing on an aid needs active balance (also in standby, since a robot cannot park on a stool). Parked standby 20 W standing = 12 W (suspended compute, wake-word DSP, one low-rate camera, BMS, network) + 8 W with the joint brakes engaged. Each active arm 40 W; holding 3 W/kg (8 kg on a 0.3 m lever is about 24 N m at the elbow, 20-30 W of copper losses); active perception 5 W; the speaker amplifier 5 W. The wheeled base balances for free.
sources.auto_standby_s: Parks after 60 s without a command, as current humanoid firmware does.
sources.walk_wh_per_m: Normal 0.288 Wh/m is navigation_robot's 0.012 %/m of 2.4 kWh (TIER1_DECISIONS): with the 70 W hotel load at 0.8 m/s the total is about 900 W, a cost of transport of about 1.8, conservative between Cassie (about 1) and ASIMO (about 3.2). Careful walking takes fewer impacts per metre, fast walking costs more per metre (cost of transport rises above the optimal speed). Wheels need about a fifth of walking's energy.
sources.load_ref_kg: Walking work x (1 + load / 40 kg): navigation_robot's carried-load rule (the arms hold the load as well as the legs carrying it).
sources.stair_wh_per_step: navigation_robot's 0.05 % up and 0.02 % down per step of a 2.4 kWh pack: lifting 60 kg by 0.18 m is 106 J of mechanical work, at the 2-3 % whole-body efficiency of a legged robot on stairs about 1 Wh; descending dissipates rather than produces energy.
sources.stair_s_per_step: 0.8 s per step: the simulator's existing stair time (core move), about 75 steps/min; adults climb at 90-100.
sources.speeds_mps: 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 m/s are the simulator's existing core SPEEDS; Figure 02 walks 1.2 m/s, Digit 1.5 m/s outdoors. The wheeled base is limited to 1.0 m/s indoors (TIAGo).
sources.decel_mps2, react_s: 0.3 s perception and control latency and 2 m/s2 braking (about 0.2 g, limited by the balance of a legged robot): stopping distances 0.16 / 0.40 / 0.72 m at careful / normal / fast speed. The wheeled base brakes at 1.5 m/s2 to avoid tipping its tall torso.
sources.noise_db_1m: Footsteps 30 / 36 / 44 dB at 1 m (navigation_robot SOUND_AT_1M_DB, the people domain's scale); quiet mode -4 dB (soft footfall, people's footstep reduction); speech 60 dB (conversation at 1 m) or 45 dB quiet; servo whine 35 dB.
sources.quiet_limit_db: 55 dB at 1 m, about a normal conversation: in quiet mode anything louder than talking is refused.
sources.charge: Constant current to 80 %, then constant voltage with an exponential taper (standard Li-ion fast charging); at the robot dock's 2 %/min (about 1.2C) 0-80 % takes 40 min and 80-99 % about 30 min. NMC cells must not charge below 0 C (lithium plating) or above 45 C, and charge at reduced current below about 10 C.
sources.pack_thermal: First-order pack temperature with tau = m c / (h A) = 14 kg x 1000 J/(kg K) / (10 W/(m2 K) x 0.8 m2) = about 1800 s; self-heating above ambient 1-8 C from standby to charging; a BMS cuts discharge at 60 C and allows it again below 50 C.
sources.energy_buffer_pct: Real packs keep a hidden reserve below the displayed 0 % for a controlled shutdown: 0.5 % of 2.4 kWh is 12 Wh, under a minute of walking or about 4 min of one-arm work.
sources.ip_rating, spray_limit_s, jet_limit_s: IP54 (Boston Dynamics Spot): dust protected and splash proof. The IPX4 test is 10 minutes of splashing (spray_limit_s 600); water jets (IPX5) are beyond the rating, so 3 s of jet already gets in.
sources.stairs: Legged robots climb stairs (one step at a time, never starting a flight the battery cannot finish); the wheeled base cannot.
sources.fault_p.gripper_slip: With a gripper_slip fault, a carried load of 1 kg or more slips out on 30 % of the walks (an assumption that makes the fault matter without making carrying useless).
